## Summary
The API uses HTTP Basic with an `InMemoryUserDetailsManager` and two local users. Moving to OAuth2 bearer tokens means a resource-server configuration, a mapping from SMART-style scopes to the existing roles, and rewritten security tests.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARC-001 | info | security | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/config/SecurityConfig.java:46 | HTTP Basic against an `InMemoryUserDetailsManager` with users `clinician` and `admin` | Replace with `oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(...))`; remove the in-memory users and `SecurityProperties` passwords. |
| ARC-002 | high | security | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/config/SecurityConfig.java:43 | `hasRole(ADMIN)` and `hasAnyRole(CLINICIAN, ADMIN)` depend on locally assigned roles | Map token scopes to roles in a `JwtAuthenticationConverter` (`user/*.read` and `user/*.write` -> CLINICIAN; an admin claim -> ADMIN). DELETE stays ADMIN-only; never trust a client-sent role claim. |
| ARC-003 | medium | testing | sample-app/src/test/java/org/example/fhir/SecurityTest.java:15 | SecurityTest authenticates with `httpBasic(...)` | Rewrite with `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt()`; keep the 401 and 403 `OperationOutcome` cases. |
| ARC-004 | low | standards | sample-app/pom.xml:43 | No `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server` dependency in pom.xml | Add it and read `issuer-uri` from an environment variable. |
